title: Distillation Without Training: Let a Strong Model Build the Weak One a Harness
hook: A strong model writes the scaffolding — code, routing, format rules — and a weak model runs inside it. Average performance nearly doubled, 0.49 to 0.91, with no parameter updates at all.
key_points: Asks whether strong-to-weak capability transfer can happen at test time instead of through training-time distillation.
A stronger 'builder' model iteratively refines an inference-time harness for a weaker target model, using 5% of the data as a validation set.
Across four Theory-of-Mind benchmarks, average target performance rose from 0.49 to 0.91 with no parameter updates.
Gains come from offloading unstable reasoning into deterministic code, benchmark-specific routing, and strict answer-format enforcement.
They do not come from making the target reason longer or sample more broadly.
Builder reasoning effort improves harness quality monotonically; the weakest target models gain the most.
content_html: Distillation normally means updating the student's weights: teacher forcing, on-policy distillation, and relatives. Cheng Qian and co-authors (arXiv, August 2026) ask whether the transfer can happen entirely at test time instead. Their setup is strong-to-weak scaffolding: a stronger builder model constructs an inference-time harness — the code, routing, and formatting around the model — and a weaker target model then solves tasks inside it, with no parameter updates.
extra_html:
Setup and result

On four representative Theory-of-Mind benchmarks, each builder uses 5% of the data as a validation set to iteratively refine its harness over several rounds; the finalized harness is then evaluated on the full test set. Average target performance nearly doubled, from 0.49 to 0.91.

Where the gains come from

The analysis matters more than the number. The improvement traces to offloading unstable model reasoning into deterministic code, benchmark-specific routing, and strict answer-format enforcement — not to coaxing the target into reasoning more extensively or sampling more widely. Builder reasoning effort improves harness quality monotonically, platform effects are modest next to the builder's own capability, and weaker targets gain the most.

The framing to take away: some of what we call "model capability" is really cognitive structure that can live outside the weights, and a strong model can write that structure down for a weaker one. Worth noting the scope — four Theory-of-Mind benchmarks, with harnesses tuned per benchmark, so how far this generalizes is still open.

related.title: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable, Navigable, and Editable
related.hook: An agent is only as good as its harness — the code that builds prompts, manages state, calls tools. The real bottleneck isn't editing that code, it's finding where a behavior lives in a huge codebase.

related.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
related.hook: A big model's softened probabilities say more than hard labels - they reveal how classes relate, so training a small model to mimic them transfers knowledge a one-hot target never could.

related.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: RL post-training gets pricier as models scale, since it needs the strong model's own rollouts. Direct-OPD reuses a cheap RL run on a small model instead, transferring the direction RL moved it.

flashcards.prompt: How does 'strong-to-weak scaffolding' differ from ordinary distillation?
flashcards.back_html: Nothing is retrained. A stronger builder model constructs an inference-time harness that a weaker target model runs inside — capability transfers as structure, not as weights.

flashcards.prompt: Where did the gains in this study actually come from?

choices.text: Offloading unstable reasoning into deterministic code, task routing, and strict answer-format enforcement
Prompting the target model to reason at much greater length
Sampling many more candidate answers and voting

flashcards.explanation_html: The analysis explicitly attributes the improvement to harness structure, not to more extensive reasoning or broader sampling by the target model.

flashcards.prompt: Which target models benefit most from a builder-designed harness?
flashcards.back_html: The weakest ones — gains are largest for weaker targets, and harness quality improves monotonically with the builder model's reasoning effort.
